strengths: The prior continuity concern is resolved for the tested interruption paths. Both 50-row long-list tests pass and keep a visible Session or People anchor within one row after same-tab reset, destination switching, detail return, and background recovery.
Horizontal ownership is clear: top controls change destinations; row swipe and long press expose only governed row actions; tested new intents return an exposed action to rest.
People Ask preserves relationship authority: multiple-context entry exposes only that person's contexts, disables Send, records zero requests, and unlocks only after an explicit relationship choice.

Session deletion is proportionate and recoverable: full-swipe deletion is disabled, confirmation names the device-local effect, cancellation changes nothing, and failed persistence restores the Session.
Artifact provenance binds the source-at-build, App, test runner, xctestrun, selected tests, result bundles, latency samples, and final screenshots.
Thirty warmed Simulator trials pass both readiness gates: destination p95 is 393.57 ms and Session-open p95 is 861.81 ms.
missing_evidence: The evidence proves deterministic Simulator behavior, not physical touch-to-photon latency, production-device gesture variance, or field performance under real recruiter data volume.
No blinded recruiter study establishes five-second findability, reduced retrieval time, lower reconstruction burden, or relationship outcome improvement.
Process termination and next-day return are not covered; only in-process destination changes, modal return, and foreground interruption are directly proven.
open_questions: Should the selected destination and visible anchor persist across process termination and next-day return, or intentionally reset to Today?
What field-study threshold will define successful retrieval for recruiters managing substantially larger live-search portfolios?
